title: Abu Bakr
hookLine: his closest friend, companion in the cave, who believed him when others called it a lie

cards: Medina, the day the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has died. The news is out, and the mosque is in uproar. Umar is on his feet, insisting it can't be true.
Then a man rides in from his home at as-Sunh, on the edge of town. He speaks to no one. He goes straight into Aisha's room, uncovers the Prophet's face, and kisses him.
Then he walks out to the crowd, and everyone waits to hear what the closest friend will say. His name is Abu Bakr.

teach.b: Bukhari records what he said. Whoever worshipped Muhammad: Muhammad has died. Whoever worships Allah: Allah is alive and does not die.
Then he recited a verse from Surah Al Imran, in Pickthall's words: "Muhammad is but a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) have passed away before him."
The report says it was as if people had never heard the verse until he recited it, and soon everyone was saying it. Umar said later that when he heard it, his legs gave way beneath him.
So who was this man, steady enough to hold a whole city on that day?

Earlier this year we heard the Prophet defend him in a quarrel, in Bukhari: when Allah sent me to you, you said, you are lying, and Abu Bakr said, he has told the truth, and he stood by me with himself and his wealth.
Will you leave my companion alone?

The tradition calls him as-Siddiq, the one who affirms the truth. In another report, the Prophet said that if he were to take an intimate friend other than his Lord, it would be Abu Bakr. Then there is the cave.

The Qur'an calls the Prophet the second of two, hiding with one companion, and commentators name that companion Abu Bakr. After the Prophet's death, the community chose Abu Bakr as caliph, to lead it.
Sunni Muslims honor him as the first of the rightly guided caliphs. Shia Muslims hold that leadership belonged to Ali, and remember these days differently. The verse he recited is the same for both.

how: Muslims remember Abu Bakr as the Prophet's companion in the cave; Sunni Muslims honor him as the first caliph and call him as-Siddiq, while Shia Muslims view the succession after the Prophet differently.

games.q: you're Abu Bakr. your closest friend has died, and the mosque is in uproar; Umar says it isn't true. you walk out to the crowd. what do you do?
o: agree with Umar, to calm everyone.
tell them he has died, and recite a verse.
games.why: he said: whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worships Allah, Allah is alive. then he recited Al Imran 144.

practice: Think of a friend who is carrying something right now: a loss, a fear, a project nobody else believes in.

Loyalty is usually small, a visit, a message that says I believe you, simply showing up when others drift away, so let one small thing come to mind for them. If you pray, ask Allah to make you a good companion to them.

wordCard.voice: Abu Bakr. The Prophet's close friend and companion in the cave, called as-Siddiq for affirming him when others called him a liar. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: one who affirms the truth; the title the tradition gives Abu Bakr.

carryVoice: Your line: the second of two. The friend who stays steady when the city shakes. Seven hundred ninety-nine days in.
